Computer models are increasingly utilized to generate data for scientific research. In hydrology, for instance, the program TOPMODEL is employed to simulate rainfall-runoff processes, producing time-series data for both inputs and outputs. This paper introduces a novel methodology for analyzing the relationship between such series using a dedicated simulator. The series are segmented into cells of fixed length, where each output cell corresponds to a specific duration, aligning with one or more corresponding input cells. The study examines the correlation between these series by calculating the cross-correlation coefficient for every cell pair. This approach allows for the quantification of the influence of various factors on a system's observed variables. The proposed technique is demonstrated using TOPMODEL simulations, and the results are contrasted with traditional analysis methods.

We introduce a new framework for robust learning that equips models with the capability to verify and identify the membership status of local data points. This framework not only enables the detection of outliers but also enhances data augmentation and improves model generalization. We begin by outlining a robust gradient descent algorithm capable of identifying local data membership. Subsequently, we examine the implications of access to local data queries for both data augmentation and generalization; specifically, we demonstrate that models trained using these queries achieve superior generalization and can be effectively regularized through robust generalization bounds. Furthermore, we leverage local membership to develop a novel iterative procedure for robust training and augmentation, ensuring resistance to both known and unforeseen forms of corruption. Empirical evaluations across various in-coupon data scenarios confirm the practical efficacy of our approach.

This study reports measurements of jet fragmentation functions within the lead-lead (PbPb) collision environment at a nucleon-nucleon center-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s_{\rm{NN}}} = 5.02$ TeV, utilizing the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider. The analysis examines pp reference samples and central PbPb events with a pseudorapidity density of $0 < | \eta | < 2.4$ and a transverse energy of $20 < E_{T}^{ \rm{ref}} < 40$ GeV. The study focuses on events with a minimum bias condition and a vertex multiplicity of $10 < N_{\rm{vtx}} < 100$. The jet fragmentation functions are determined as a function of the scalar jet energy, ranging from 20 to 40 GeV, and the transverse momenta of resulting hadrons relative to the jet axis, with fractional momentum $0.1 < z < 0.9$. These results are contrasted with those from proton-proton interactions at the same center-of-m energies but at different collision energies. The study reveals a suppression of jet fragmentation functions in central PbPb events compared to pp collisions, specifically for $E_{T}^{ \rm{ref}} < 20$ GeV, which is interpreted as the effect of the dense QCD medium.

Inverse Ap\'{e}ry-type (or binomial series) have become increasingly popular tools for high-precision numerical computation. In this paper, we derive several new identities involving Ap\'{e}ry-type binomial series. These results generalize multiple known combinatorial and (or) $${\pi}$$-expansion theorems.

This study reports the discovery of a new, extremely red, isolated Y dwarf, designated YW J0523-0810, with a WISE $W1-W2$ color index of 5.07 and a $W2-W3$ index of 1.05. This object exhibits the most red $W1-W2$ color among all known Y dwarfs. Its spectral features are consistent with those of Y0d subdwarfs, specifically lacking the CH$_4$ absorption seen in other Y0d objects and showing unusually weak NH$_3$ absorption. Additionally, YW J0523-0810 is the only known Y dwarf with a $W2-W3$ index exceeding 1.0. Its position in the $W1-W2$ versus $W2-W3$ color-color diagram suggests it may represent a unique object within the Y dwarf population. The object's age is estimated to be 1.0 Gyr, and its effective temperature is approximately 450 K.

We report on the measurement of radial flow in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}=7$ TeV, using events with varying charged-particle multiplicities ($2 < \text{ch} < 2000$) detected by the ALICE experiment at the LHC. This flow characterization is derived from the transverse momentum spectra of particles across the entire spectrum, as well as from the particle number and transverse momentum averages. The observed trends in both the multiplicity and average $p_T$ distributions align with findings from previous measurements in proton-proton and heavy-ion collisions. These results are compared to predictions from various event-by-event hydrodynamic models, revealing that such frameworks successfully describe the measured behavior in high-multiplicity proton-proton collisions.

This paper introduces a methodology for generating synthetic proton datasets using the Tevatron's detector configuration. We employ this technique to evaluate various parts of the nucleus function (PDF) fitting strategies. Since PDFs characterize the internal structure of the proton and are essential for predicting outcomes in proton-proton collisions, this work aims to illustrate how synthetic data can effectively support PDF analysis.

Although prior research has extensively examined the 3D printing of metal and ceramic materials using regolith simulants, investigations into the printability of actual extraterrestrial regolith remain scarce. This study evaluates the 3D printability of Martian and Lunar regolith by employing a direct ink writing technique with a polylactic acid binder. Printed structures were subsequently subjected to sintering to enhance their mechanical properties, with microstructural and mechanical analyses performed on the resulting samples. The study demonstrates that both Martian and Lunar regolith can be successfully 3D printed, yielding structures with comparable initial mechanical characteristics. Sintering optimizes these mechanical properties; however, achieving the necessary compressive strength requires temperatures exceeding 1000°C for both Martian and Lunar regolith. Notably, the samples derived from Lunar regolith exhibit superior mechanical performance and microstructural quality compared to those from Martian regolith across all tested conditions. These findings suggest that 3D printing could serve as a viable method for in-situ production of structural materials during future space exploration missions.

This study investigates the instability of a liquid film flowing along a fiber, a system modeled by the classic Rayleigh-Lamb equation. The analysis focuses on how a slip condition at the liquid-solid interface influences the system, a factor often neglected in prior research that assumed no-slip conditions. By employing a perturbation approach to derive a slip-dependent base flow profile, the authors calculate the growth rate of disturbances for various slip magnitudes. The findings reveal that slip facilitates faster growth, with a optimal slip value producing the maximum amplification; however, the observed instability remains consistent with the classical no-slip scenario in terms of overall behavior. Additionally, a linear stability analysis was conducted to corroborate these findings, with the study's predictions showing strong agreement with previous numerical simulations reported in the literature.

We introduce the first detection of the Br$\gamma$ hydrogen recombination line in the nearby starburst galaxy NGC 4933, utilizing the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA). Our data reveal a Br$\gamma$ flux of $1.1 \pm 0.2$ Jy km s$^{-1}$, which corresponds to a star formation rate (SFR) of $1.1 \pm 0.2$ M$_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$. This Br$\gamma$-derived SFR is consistent with the Br$\alpha$-based SFR of $1.0 \pm 0.2$ M$_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$ previously reported by Kewley et al. (2004), and both values align well with the SFR estimated from H$_2$O masers ($1.0 \pm 0.2$ M$_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$) and the Br$\alpha$ measurement. Additionally, ALMA's high-resolution capabilities allow us to map the Br$\gamma$ emission, showing a spatial distribution that closely matches the distribution of star formation derived from submillimeter data.

This article investigates the categories local modules and braided auto-equivalences for $D_{10}$-symmetric fusion categories. We identify four exceptional cases involving $D_{10}$-symmetric fusion categories, within of which the braided auto-equivalences local modules can be systematically classified. For all other fusion categories exhibiting $D_{10}$-symmetry, these braided auto-equivalences local modules are constructed from permutations of simple object isomorphism types alongside local braided auto-equivalences of those simple objects.

The Fisher-KPP equation, recognized for describing the propagation of traveling fronts associated with genetic or demographic selection during the expansion of populations, is extended here into a non-local form. This extension involves the integration of an exponential kernel, which induces exponential decay at infinity and permits for longer-range interactions. Through the application of the dual formulation, we demonstrate that in the long-time limit, the leading edge of the support of these solutions decays more rapidly than previously observed local cases. Furthermore, by employing a rescaling technique, we establish the existence of self-similar solutions that characterize the system's asymptotic behavior.

We introduce a new dataset comprising handwritten historical documents from the early 20th century, featuring transcribed Italian and Spanish mathematical terms. We analyze these scripts using binary image representations and provide detailed labels for each term based on its subject area. We release this data to enable researchers to develop automatic classifiers that identify the mathematical domain of written terms. Specifically, we create a machine learning model that discriminates between "relevant" and "irrelevant" terms for a given field. We evaluate the model's performance across various learning methods and demonstrate that neural networks achieve superior results.

This study investigates the effectiveness of modeling speech synthesis duration using statistics other than the traditional conditional mean. Although current neural TTS predominantly relies on generating the conditional mean for duration, this work explores whether alternative probability distribution metrics, such as the median or mode, yield superior results. The authors present a new approach that models duration as the median via a quantile network, contrasting this with standard error metrics like mean squared error. When evaluated on the LJSpeech dataset, this proposed method outperforms a standard baseline by improving mean conditional log-likelihood (mNLL) scores. Additionally, the study analyzes the characteristics of the resulting synthesized waveforms to provide insights into the nature of duration modeling using these alternative statistical measures.

Ecological research frequently relies on count data, such as that gathered through visual surveys or acoustic sensors, to investigate species distributions and abundances. These count records are typically influenced by unobserved variables, including observer skill, environmental conditions, and the number of samples observed. Consequently, estimated species distributions may fail to accurately reflect true abundances, especially when sampling is sparse. This study presents a Bayesian approach utilizing a latent class framework to estimate the number of classes and their respective abundances directly from count data. Our method accounts for variations in detection probability caused by unobserved factors, including the latent class itself. We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach through a simulation study and by applying it to a real-world dataset concerning bird calls recorded via automated acoustic monitoring devices.

Malignant skin lesions are a prevalent global health issue, and early detection is crucial for improving patient outcomes. While deep learning has shown great promise in diagnosis, it often struggles with ambiguity when facing difficult cases. To address this, we introduce a new interactive deep learning framework designed to aid in the classification of such lesions. Our system operates through two sequential stages: first, it automatically identifies and segments candidate regions within an image; second, it generates multiple classification predictions for those regions, each accompanied by a confidence score. To facilitate user interaction, the system allows users to select one of these predictions for final adoption or to request additional suggestions if needed. By iteratively refining choices through user feedback, the framework delivers a set of classification results with higher certainty. Extensive testing across two datasets, the ISIC 2018 Challenge and the ISIC 2018/19 Challenge datasets, demonstrates that this approach outperforms several established baseline methods.

We introduce a probabilistic autoencoder designed for type Ia supernova (SN Ia) spectral data, utilizing a physically-parameterized framework to decode observed spectra. This model incorporates a probabilistic framework to handle spectral noise and employs a parameterized principal component analysis (PCA) basis to represent spectral variability. By using PCA, we achieve a basis that is both compact and computationally efficient. Our approach is grounded in a physical model of SN Ia, allowing the probabilistic autoencoder to extract these spectra from actual observational datasets. We validate the method using spectral time-series data from the SALT2 model, demonstrating that the autoencoder recovers the underlying parameters accurately. Furthermore, we apply the technique to reconstruct spectra derived from SALT2 observations, successfully retrieving the true parameters embedded within the simulated data. When tested with real observational spectra, the autoencoder successfully identifies plausible physical parameters, although these results exhibit a bias that we discuss in detail. Finally, we outline potential future applications for this physics-informed, compression-efficient methodology.

We report the detection of a massive neutral gas outflow in the Dusty Star-Forming Galaxy HATLASJ08538.9+015537 (hereafter referred to as DSFG), a galaxy identified via a 1.1 mm continuum emission peak at a redshift of $z=2.15$. Utilizing ALMA observations of the $^{12}$CO(3-2) transition, we determined an atomic gas mass of approximately $1.5 \times 10^{10} M_{\odot}$ for this outflow. The outflow's kinematics are characterized by a deprojected velocity of $180 \pm 20$ km s$^{-1}$ and a velocity dispersion of $100 \pm 10$ km s$^{-1}$. The outflow's physical dimensions are estimated at roughly 1.5 kpc, with a mass outflow rate of $\dot{M}_{\rm out} \approx 1.5 M_{\odot} yr^{-1}$. The CO luminosity of the outflow is approximately 10% of that of the host galaxy, while the CO-to-H$_2$ mass conversion factor is roughly 10% lower than the host's value. The outflow's mass outflow rate exceeds the star formation rate by a factor of approximately 10, suggesting that a significant portion

This study investigates the entrainment of ambient fluid by an axisymmetric turbulent plume carrying suspended particles, utilizing direct numerical simulations. The research demonstrates that the direction of buoyancy fluxes significantly influences the entrainment rate. Specifically, upward-moving plumes exhibit a higher entrainment ratio compared to downward-moving ones when the magnitude of the buoyancy flux remains constant. Furthermore, the study reveals that the orientation of the mean plume axis affects the entrainment rate in both upward and downward configurations. The findings indicate that for a fixed initial momentum flux, a deviation of the plume axis toward a horizontal orientation enhances entrainment in both directions. The study attributes these phenomena to variations in the vertical profile of the mean axial velocity and the redistribution of the buoyancy field, which alter the radial gradients of the mean axial velocity. Consequently, changes in the radial shear of the mean flow modulate the entrainment process.

Diseases spread through intricate networks defined by individual contacts, prompting researchers to investigate how network topology influences epidemic dynamics. While extensive work has examined graphs that represent these contacts, such models often fail to capture the simultaneous, multi-way interactions between groups of people. This work proposes an alternative using contact hypergraphs to more accurately reflect interaction-heavy social behaviors. By conducting a detailed analysis of the mean-field dynamics for an $SIR$ epidemic on these hypergraphs, the study derives a corresponding set of stochastic dynamics. Furthermore, the paper presents a simulation-based algorithm to generate realistic contact hypergraphs. The findings indicate that an epidemic's trajectory is profoundly shaped by both the nature of multi-way interactions and the specific hypergraph contact structure. Ultimately, the authors demonstrate that utilizing contact hypergraphs offers a superior framework for modeling how infections propagate through populations.

The recent discovery of two-dimensional magnetic semiconductors, exemplified by CrI$_3$, has sparked significant research into their spintronic applications. In this study, we employ a first-principles approach to examine spin-polarized transport in two-dimensional CrI$_3$. Our analysis reveals that spin canting effects, inherent to the magnetic order in this material, can be clearly distinguished from the spin-polarized transport properties. Furthermore, we explore the potential for controlling magnetization orientation through external electric fields, demonstrating the capacity to switch between metallic and insulating states. These findings underscore the promising spintronic potential of atomically thin CrI$_3$.

This study investigates magnetic dynamos in solar-like stars using the widely used, yet unverified, $\Omega$-effect model. By varying the Rossby number ($Ro$) from 0.1 to 10, we explore how differential rotation influences the $Ro$-dependence of magnetic activity. Our findings reveal a flat $Ro$-dependence for magnetic activity, consistent with observations, but a strong $Ro$-dependence for differential rotation, creating a discrepancy that challenges the validity of the $\alpha$-$\Omega$ effect model.

Multimodal learning addresses how to effectively integrate information from diverse sources, such as text, audio, and visuals. While existing autoencoder techniques for learning shared representations often rely on predefined structures, our work introduces a K-fan deep model capable of handling arbitrary numbers of inputs and outputs. This architecture utilizes multiple branches to process distinct modalities independently before merging them via attention mechanisms to emphasize significant features. Our model also incorporates a variational autoencoder framework to facilitate latent space manipulation, supporting downstream tasks like generation and editing. Additionally, we develop a specialized branch for handling K-fan inputs, enabling the direct encoding and decoding of visual elements, including images and 3D shapes.

This paper introduces a novel approach to automatically generate property-based tests for Java programs, specifically targeting multi-threaded applications where conventional testing methods fall short. While unit tests focus excessively on individual components and functional tests rely on developer-provided scenarios that are difficult to scale for complex state, functional testing via asserted invariants offers a promising alternative. However, creating these tests manually is impractical for programs with complex execution flows, necessitating automated generation. Our solution utilizes a Deep Reinforcement Learning model to autonomously discover test invariants, which are subsequently verified using a static analysis tool. This method successfully identifies numerous test invariants in multi-threaded Java code, including properties that evade detection by both standard testing frameworks and prope

WhatsApp's popularity stems from its ability to facilitate direct messaging and content sharing within private, closed networks. Unfortunately, this environment has enabled the swift propagation of misinformation, often accompanied by manipulative tactics like fabricated sender identities to encourage interaction. Although information verification systems exist, their effectiveness is limited by users' reluctance to engage with others to confirm facts. This paper introduces a novel framework for detecting misinformation on WhatsApp by analyzing the linguistic features of the content itself, the associated Arabic dialect, and the metadata. The study utilizes both supervised and unsupervised machine learning techniques to identify false narratives. The results indicate that the proposed system achieves an accuracy of 92.81%, demonstrating the significant potential of metadata in uncovering the content's authenticity.

We introduce a model of a branching population in which individuals of a specific type $i$ mutate into type $j$ at a rate proportional to $\lambda_{ij} n^{ -\alpha }$, where population size $n$ denotes the count of individuals of type $i$. This interaction is mediated by a "common environment" that fluctuates randomly over time according to a continuous-time random walk. The study characterizes the limiting behavior of the system as both population sizes and time scale tend to infinity. A defining feature of this model is its frequency spectrum, which represents the ordered distribution of type frequencies within the population. This spectrum converges to a limit that fluctuates stochastically as time progresses. These fluctuations are driven by the shared environmental changes and can be described by a non-Markovian stochastic process. The long-term dynamics of this process depend critically on the parameter $\alpha$: when $\alpha < 1/2$, the frequencies stabilize at a deterministic average, whereas for $\alpha > 1/2$, the system exhibits random behavior.

This paper introduces a deep neural network (DNN)-based spoofing detection system that utilizes attention rectified linear units (ARAESU) alongside the attention mechanism. The core of this framework is the AReLU, which integrates attention directly into rectified linear units to produce variable rectification factors contingent upon input data. By dynamically adjusting the rectification based on input features, AReLU enhances the model's ability to concentrate on critical information. Experimental results indicate that systems employing AReLU outperform traditional models using standard rectified linear units (ReLU), demonstrating superior performance in spoofing detection.

Supergravity (SUGRA) presents significant challenges when building inflationary models. This paper examines a class of homogeneous K\"ahler potentials that are compatible with SUGRA frameworks and capable supporting inflation. We demonstrate that these models support slow-roll inflation within a regime where the SUGRA contribution remains negligible, allowing for a precise calculation of all relevant observables. Furthermore, by analyzing the effects of the SUGRA regime on these specific K\"ahler potentials, we identify viable models capable of driving natural inflation.

This study examines nonreciprocity in the two-photon quantum correlations of dual-photon states exiting a fiber Bragg grating (FBG) based nonlininiral optical loop mirror (OLM). We observe that while the nonlininirality of single-photon probabilities remains constant for both co- and counter-propagating directions within the FBG-OLM setup, the two-photon correlation nonlininirality varies with direction. Specifically, the two-photon state can undergo a complete reversal in correlation character—from anti-coherent to coherent—depending solely on the propagation direction. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the magnitude of single-photon nonlininirality serves to regulate the two-photon correlation nonlinirality and nonlininirality. These findings provide novel perspectives for understanding quantum light statistics and nonlininirality, with promising applications in the transmission of multi-photon quantum information and the development of new quantum technologies.

Superconducting quantum circuits have emerged as a leading platform for quantum computation, attracting significant research interest. However, the scaling of this technology is hindered by material flaws within the fabrication processes. This study investigates how fabrication errors in quantum dot-based superconducting quantum circuits impact multi-qubit entanglement. We demonstrate that even minor defects in the quantum well can drastically reduce entanglement among distant qubits by inducing charge noise in the quantum dot spin qubits. Our findings underscore the critical necessity of mitigating fabrication errors to enable the large-scale production of superconducting quantum computers.

We examine infinite collections of maps, known as self-mappings, applied to the positive half-line that produce any given countable partition of it into Borel sets. This investigation extends the classical partitional framework initiated by Hausdorff, which demonstrated the feasibility of partitioning the real line into un-Borel sets under specific cardinal assumptions, and one that was further generalized by Silver. Our analysis surpasses previous work by Kechris, Magee, and Miller, offering a solution under minimal assumptions regarding cardinality. The investigation is concluded with an example illustrating a countable arrangement of maps whose fixed ranges generate a partition wherein every equivalence class is classified as analytic but not Borel.

Commodity Trading Advisors (CTAs) are prominent figures in financial markets, renowned for achieving consistent long-term profits through trading strategies that span various horizons. This study investigates the hypothesis that these successes stem not merely from the CTA's own skill, but from inducing short-term reversal traders to act against one another. Specifically, we examine whether the market activity generated by such traders creates conditions favorable to profitable strategies based on price convergence. Our analysis reveals that CTA performance is significantly enhanced by the presence of short-term reversal activity, a benefit that is most pronounced when traders exhibit low sentiment. Furthermore, we observe that the market activity spurred by these short-term players facilitates the development of profitable long-horizon convergence strategies.

Protocol analysis serves as a fundamental technique in monitoring network security, yet it faces significant difficulties in accurately determining the protocol type, particularly within encrypted traffic where the content remains opaque. While deep learning offers a promising pathway for protocol identification, current methods face limitations such as the high cost of training, the need for specific input data, and the lack of adaptability to new environments. To address these issues, this paper introduces a Protocol Discovery mechanism utilizing Transfer Learning. This approach streamlines the determination process by eliminating the need for deep learning models to re-train from scratch, thereby enhancing the speed and efficiency of protocol detection. Our method is evaluated using the Emnist dataset, demonstrating a top-1 Protocol Discovery accuracy of 98.12% and a top-5 accuracy of 99.81%.

This study presents a comprehensive theoretical analysis of magnon transport in twisted bilayer magnetic insulators, focusing on systems with on-site and nearest-neighbor anisotropies. By employing a tight-binding framework, we examine how moiré flat bands form and investigate the characteristics of magnon wavefunctions. Furthermore, we utilize a Boltzmann transport equation to evaluate the electrical resistivity and thermal conductivity associated with spin and magnetization degrees of freedom. Our findings indicate that magnons serve as promising carriers for information, demonstrating the potential for efficient thermal conductivity alongside the enablement of coupled spin and orbital currents.

Federated learning (FL) has emerged as a promising approach for training machine learning models, offering enhanced privacy by avoiding the transfer of sensitive user data and ensuring robustness against biased data through decentralized aggregation. However, current aggregation techniques often overlook the impact of data heterogeneity, leading to suboptimal performance. This paper introduces a novel model and adaptive aggregation strategy that incorporates a quantized communication channel to enhance FL efficacy while minimizing bandwidth usage. The proposed method utilizes a quantized logarithmic Mitchell-Orr (Q-MIT) optimizer for local updates and a generalized quantized Federated Averaging (GfedAvg) scheme for server-side aggregation. Additionally, we derive a new communication complexity bound for this framework, demonstrating that the quantized Q-MIT+GfedAvg system offers superior accuracy compared to standard federated averaging under constraints of heterogeneous data and limited communication capacity.

This Letter introduces a theoretical framework for analyzing the generation of high-dimensional Greenberger-Horne-Zeinberger (GHZ) resources. The study focuses on entanglement purity as a key metric for evaluating the quality of these non-classical states. The proposed method is validated through the experimental generation of $N$-partite GHZ states across dimensions up to $d=4$. The study concludes by outlining the significant potential of entanglement purity as a benchmark to guide the production of superior high-dimensional GHZ states.

This paper investigates uplink channel estimation for non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) systems enhanced with intelligent-reflecting-surface (IRS). We propose a maximum likelihood (ML) joint estimation method for the IRS configuration and user channels, which, due to the non-convex nature of the associated optimization problem, is solved via an alternating optimization (AO) approach. Within this framework, user channel estimation employs sparse learning techniques, while IRS phase matrix estimation utilizes sequential AO combined with semidefinite relaxation (SDR). Furthermore, we introduce a novel scheme that leverages prior NOMA user channel knowledge to streamline uplink channel estimation by facilitating a direct, single-shot ML approach when estimating the IRS phase matrix. Simulation results demonstrate that our methods significantly outperform conventional baseline schemes in terms of total estimation error.

Between March and May 2020, we analyzed 1.1 million articles from the New York Times and USA Today to examine how local news coverage of COVID-19 evolved in relation to national death rates. Although the volume of coverage initially surged, it declined over time, yet remained substantial even as the United States approached its peak in national fatalities. Spatially, the intensity of reporting varied significantly by locality, often diverging from regional infection and mortality statistics. Furthermore, the angle of coverage shifted, moving from a focus on the virus's origins and spread to an emphasis on government responses and the virus's impact on individuals. These findings suggest that media attention on COVID-19 was sustained throughout the critical early phase of the pandemic, irrespective of rising death tolls, and that the contextual framing of the story underwent a distinct transformation.

"Learning to count" refers to the gradual acquisition of counting abilities, a process marked by distinct phases, milestones, and critical transition points known as "inflection points." An inflection point signifies a moment where ability levels undergo a qualitative transformation, often accompanied by a sudden surge in performance. This study investigates the nature of the "learn-to-count" process by analyzing individual trajectories in subitizing—the immediate perception of small quantities—as illustrated through longitudinal data from the "Children's Bookshelf" project. We observe that subitizing performance does not improve gradually; instead, it progresses via discrete jumps, characterized by abrupt transitions triggered at specific ages. These transitions are well-modeled by a logistic function, with parameters that remain consistent across different demographic groups. Furthermore, the intervals between these inflection points exhibit variability but generally adhere to a log-normal distribution. The findings suggest that ability development in young children is best understood as a series of discontinuous leaps rather than a continuous flow.

Bloom filters serve as a space-efficient method for checking element inclusion in a set, but they lack the ability to confirm an element's absence. Cuckoo filters address this limitation by supporting definite negative results, yet their positive detection accuracy is constrained. To enhance the precision of positive matches in cuckoo filters, we introduce a novel technique called "fingerprinting," which leverages additional stored data to significantly reduce false positives. This approach preserves all standard cuckoo filter traits—specifically constant space usage for constant query time, the ability to definitively rule out elements, and constant storage overhead relative to the set size—while achieving dramatically higher verification accuracy for present items.

We introduce a market model where the future price depends on current trading volume during a specific time interval, creating a feedback loop between price and action. This environment is explored using both Brownian motion and a discrete-time framework. We provide specific trading strategies that guarantee a global set of prices over time, allowing agents to achieve arbitrary cumulative profits by repeating these methods indefinitely.

This study introduces Federated Learning with Local Stochastic Proximal Gradient (FLLSPG), a novel approach designed to ensure privacy while remaining robust against Byzantine attacks. By executing local stochastic proximal gradient updates on the client side, the proposed method introduces a regularization term that simultaneously protects data confidentiality and filters out malicious influences. Additionally, the server adopts a median-based selector to further mitigate Byzantine attacks. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that FLLSPG achieves global optimality and provides comprehensive proofs regarding convergence and privacy guarantees. Experimental results confirm that the algorithm effectively withstands various Byzantine attack scenarios and delivers efficient, high-privacy federated learning.

We propose a novel approach to autonomous driving by employing reinforcement learning to instruct an agent in learning to drive within a deep learning-based, end-to-end simulation environment. This deep neural network-based driving simulator accepts raw camera imagery as input and outputs control commands. Training aims to maximize the cumulative reward over time by optimizing a reward function designed to encourage safe, collision-free navigation. To achieve this, we utilize a multi-agent setup where one agent acts as the vehicle and additional agents simulate obstacles, allowing for the generation of diverse training scenarios. By integrating a reward mechanism that evaluates collisions with these virtual objects, the system effectively trains the single-agent vehicle controller.

Recent advancements in deep learning have facilitated the creation of highly realistic synthetic faces, commonly referred to as deepfakes. Although these deepfakes offer promising applications, they also pose significant security risks. This paper provides an overview of current deepfake generation methods alongside various detection strategies.

The discovery of thousands of exoplanets has intensified the search for Earth-like worlds, specifically those with liquid water oceans and habitable temperatures. While the minimum mass required to generate an atmosphere is well-understood, the upper mass limit for potential habitability remains uncertain. This study investigates the relationship between planetary mass and the presence of surface oceans, utilizing an Earth-like atmosphere and composition as a baseline. We demonstrate that sub-Neptune-sized exoplanets, which are the most prevalent class detected so far, can theoretically sustain liquid water oceans if their gaseous envelopes constitute less than approximately 0.1% of their total mass. Furthermore, we analyze the impact of internal heat sources on atmospheric expansion, showing that habitable surface conditions are more likely on planets orbiting their host stars at greater distances. Finally, we assess the effects of water's supercritical state on planetary structure and confirm that planets with masses exceeding roughly 10 Earth-meters cannot maintain surface oceans.

This study investigates the capacity of binary connected spiking neurons to acquire temporal sequences using a novel unsupervised learning framework. We demonstrate that an asymmetrical weight structure is crucial for effective sequence learning in this setup. Through theoretical analysis, we show that with suitably chosen synapses, these networks can perfectly represent arbitrary sequences as Trepiccov chains by matching the network's transition probabilities to those of the target model. We further provide numerical evidence confirming the robustness of these networks against noise in pre-synaptic activity and target statistics. Last, we illustrate the application of this mechanism to successfully encode musical rhythms.

Existing OCR systems often struggle with generalization to unseen text instances not encountered during training, a limitation that becomes especially critical in Autonomous Driving (AD) contexts where diverse, unseen text types are ubiquitous. Although recent advances in OCR rely heavily on pre-training with extensive datasets, these approaches often fail to adequately address the specific challenges of detecting and recognizing novel text. To bridge this gap, we introduce a generalized pre-training strategy specifically for ad-text, which targets both detection and recognition of ad-text while enhancing domain adaptability. Our method introduces a unified framework capable of handling diverse categories, including scene text and ad-text, by employing a multi-task learning approach. Additionally, we develop a self-supervised technique to identify and remove fraudulent ad-text from sources, thereby preventing the model from learning misleading patterns. Extensive experiments across multiple datasets demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art methods in generalization ability. Source code will be made publicly available.

The paper demonstrates how generalized polynomial chaos (gPC) expansion serves as an efficient technique for solving differential equations with random coefficients. By introducing the method through a linear advection case, it establishes the procedure for deriving the gPC coefficients utilizing a collocation approach. Although the discussion remains confined to constant coefficient differential equations, it highlights that the framework extends readily to variable coefficients.

In industrial settings, sensor networks frequently generate vast, high-dimensional data streams that demand real-time processing. Within this context, the real-time monitoring of these high-dimensional data streams becomes a critical challenge. This study introduces a dimensionality reduction technique for monitoring multi-variate control charts, specifically designed for continuous, high-velocity data flows. The proposed method constructs the statistical properties of the data using a dynamic kernel, enabling the simultaneous dimensionality reduction and monitoring. The effectiveness of this approach is validated through a case study on a cement mill, with further statistical evidence supporting its applicability.

We introduce a novel method for calculating infall timescales by analyzing the full phase-space distribution of accreted stellar populations. This approach is applied to two major Milky Way merger remnants: the Gaia-Sausage Enceladus dwarf galaxy and the LMS-1 (Wukong) dwarf spheroidal. By modeling the kinematics of these systems as anisotropic, collisionless, steady-state, axisymmetric distributions, we derive characteristic e-folding timescales of approximately 2.0 ± 0.3 Gyr for GSE and 2.2 ± 0.3 Gyr for Wukong. These values indicate that both features formed prior to the cessation of their respective accretion events, implying that the observed kinematic signatures were modified by the evolution of the host galaxy after the merger concluded.

Consider a compact topological space $X$ with profinite homotopy groups and a profinite group $G$ acting continuously on $X$. This study establishes a convergence theorem for the homotopy orbits of $G$ acting on $X$, utilizing the homotopy groups of $X$ as coefficients. Specifically, it is shown that the homotopy groups of the homotopy orbits fit within an $E^2$-page of the homotopy groups of $X$ as the first term of the spectral sequence, provided the $G$-module structure on the homotopy groups of $X$ meets a specific finiteness criterion.

When $G$ is a profinite group and $X$ is a pro-$\mathbb{Z}$-simplicial set whose homotopy groups are discrete and finitely generated, an analogous result holds. In this setting, the $E^\infty$-page of the spectral sequence, with $E^2$-page matching the first continuous spectral sequence with coefficients in the homotopy groups of $X$, yields the homotopy groups of the homotopy orbits of $G$ acting on $X$.

In recent times, the proliferation of digital documents has spurred significant interest in automatic information extraction systems. Among these, extracting data from invoices presents a formidable challenge due to variations in layout, the complexity of value calculations, and the intricacy of tax regulations. Although numerous studies have attempted to develop extraction models, they typically rely on standardized templates that fail to accommodate distinct visual styles. Consequently, creating models capable of handling varying layouts demands extensive manual effort to annotate documents, resulting in high costs and prolonged development cycles. To overcome this limitation, this paper introduces a new approach for extracting information from invoices that minimizes the reliance on heavily annotated training data. The study evaluates the model's performance by analyzing the quantity of fully annotated samples, demonstrating that it effectively handles diverse layout styles even when trained primarily on documents of a single layout.

The EuS/InAs interface is investigated as a prospective spin-orbit torque (STT) device utilizing EuS as a spin detector. We analyze various configurations, specifically examining how the EuS valence band maximum aligns with the InAs valence band maximum, as well as different bonding setups. Our findings reveal that in all scenarios, EuS forms a thin surface layer on InAs, and the EuS valence band maximum sits approximately 0.5 eV below the InAs counterpart. Additionally, the analysis of bonding types and their resulting electronic structures indicates that the most favorable configuration involves hydrogen bonding between Eu and InAs, a structure that maintains the intrinsic electronic properties of both materials.

We introduce ClickTrain, a novel framework designed to accelerate convolutional neural network (CNN) training by leveraging click maps that encode pixel-level object boundaries. By optimizing only the network's convolutional filters in an end-to-end manner using these maps as training signals, ClickTrain eliminates the dependency on hand-crafted ImageNet training protocols, including random cropping, data augmentation, and supervised back-propagation through labels. Experiments demonstrate that models trained with ClickTrain achieve top-tier performance on COCO for instance segmentation and on ADE200 for semantic segmentation, all while training exclusively using pixel-wise boundary annotations.

This study explores bounded distributive residuated lattices and their Boolean lexicographic products. We introduce a method to generate subresiduated lattices through the ordered subsets of their canonical extensions, demonstrating that every bounded distributive residuation lattice can be represented in this manner. Furthermore, we investigate the properties of the MacNeille completion alongside the structured extension approach applied to both bounded and distributive residuation lattices.

Gravitational wave observatories such as LIGO and Virgo have identified signals from three distinct sources: compact binary coalescences involving black holes, neutron stars, or mixed black hole-neon star systems. While the binary black hole merger rate is anticipated to be the most prevalent, recent detections of neutron stars have spurred efforts to identify additional neutron stars within these binaries. This study proposes a new method to detect neutron stars hidden within gravitational wave compact binary coalescence signals. Utilizing Bayesian inference, we analyze simulated data generated from a mixture of three models: binary black hole mergers, binary neutron star mergers, and binary black hole-neon star pairs. Our results indicate that the mixture model successfully identifies neutron stars in 90% of cases where they constitute 10% of the total population, achieving a detection efficiency of nearly 100% when neutron stars comprise half the dataset. These findings suggest that incorporating expected neutron star signals into the analysis of binary black hole events offers a promising avenue for discovering currently undetected neutron stars.

The discovery of the Sun's unexpected lack of giant planets has prompted numerous studies investigating the host-star metallicity connection with this missing population. This work presents the first analysis of the Gaia Early Data Release 3 (EDR3) catalog, which includes 1,011 G-type stars with confirmed giant planets. We identify 1,011 G-type host stars surrounding giant planets and find that the median metallicity of these stars is 0.1 dex below the solar value, though a slight positive correlation exists between host metallicity and the metallicity of the giant planets themselves. Additionally, we find no significant link between host metallicity and the mass of the giant planet. By comparing our findings with previous literature, we observe consistent results, yet our study offers the most precise metallicity measurements to date for a large sample of giant-planet-hosting stars.

This paper addresses the optimal control of a single agent operating within a Markov Decision Process (MDP) framework subject to both terminal and path-based state and action constraints. These constraints are implemented using a Lagrangian approach that incorporates multiple random sampling points to maintain feasibility. By integrating this with a neural network-based function approximation, the study introduces a deep learning-based algorithm capable of handling these requirements effectively. The framework is particularly well-suited for operations management scenarios involving state or action limitations, such as inventory systems with capacity restrictions or dynamic pricing models constrained by minimum or maximum bounds. The paper validates the proposed methodology through simulations on a deep learning-primal dual algorithm applied to a pricing CMDP with terminal constraints, demonstrating superior performance compared to standard MDP techniques when both optimal pricing and floor/ceiling constraints are considered.

Handwritten text recognition has been extensively studied, particularly in the field of handwritten mathematical expression recognition (HMER). While HMER systems have achieved significant performance gains, the majority focus on character classification, often overlooking symbol segmentation. Segmentation is a critical initial step in many expression recognition pipelines, yet it faces unique hurdles specific to mathematics, including the varied connectivity of characters, complex structural details, and the high sensitivity of the task to segmentation inaccuracies. This paper introduces a novel deep convolutional neural network designed specifically for automatically segmenting handwritten symbols within expressions. By leveraging a multi-scale architecture, the proposed method effectively captures both fine-grained symbol details and the overall expression context to enhance segmentation precision. Additionally, a handcrafted prior is integrated to refine the output further. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach outperforms existing methods on the standard CROHME-HM dataset.

We investigate superconformal quantum mechanics defined on a resolved Calabi-Yau two-fold, denoted as $\tilde{X}$, with resolution parameter $h=0$. In this framework, BPS states correspond precisely to twisted Dolbeault cohomology classes on $\tilde{X}$. By utilizing the conformal quantum mechanics formalism, we derive a formula for the BPS index of specific classes within this superqum. This formula explicitly accounts for the contributions of isolated fixed points and one-dimensional orbits under the $SU(2)$ conformal group's action. The result successfully reproduces the expected BPS spectrum for $\tilde{X}$, including the resolution contributions.

This paper examines the long-term behavior of an epidemic model operating on a heterogeneous network, where the structure is represented by a connected, undirected, and unweighted graph. Unlike previous research that typically assumes uniform or exponentially distributed node degrees, our analysis accommodates arbitrary distributions of node connectivity. We establish that the network's heterogeneous structure significantly alters epidemic dynamics in the mean-field limit, often resulting in higher prevalence levels compared to homogeneous systems with equivalent average degrees. Furthermore, our findings indicate a strong correlation between the variability of node degrees and the peak density of infected individuals during an outbreak. By extending the standard contact process to include arbitrary degree distributions, we derive sufficient conditions for both the initial and secondary growth stages of infection. Additionally, we investigate how local and global recovery mechanisms influence infection spread, demonstrating that local recovery tends to amplify the epidemic's reach, whereas global recovery restricts it.

Actor-critic (AC) reinforcement learning (RL) has become a standard approach for addressing sequential decision-making problems. However, the convergence of AC algorithms is often compromised by the difficulty of learning an accurate critic, a problem exacerbated in high-dimensional settings. We introduce Hamiltonian Actor-Critic (HAC), which incorporates Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) within the policy gradient framework to enhance both the efficiency of gradient descent for optimizing the policy and the sample efficiency of the value function approximation through amortized variational inference. By integrating a continuous-time dynamics perspective into ac structures, our method exploits the geometric properties of the underlying function spaces to facilitate more effective policy search. Extensive experiments across diverse environments, including discrete and continuous MDPs, demonstrate that HAC consistently outperforms current state-of-the-art methods.

For any integer $n \geq 2$, the set of prime numbers is denoted by $\mathcal{P}_n = \{p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_n\} = \{2, 3, \ldots, p_n\}$, arranged in ascending order. Since every prime greater than or equal to 5 assumes the form $6k \pm 1$, we can express $p_n$ as $6k_n + \varepsilon_n$, where $k_n \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\varepsilon_n \in \{-1, 1\}$. This paper establishes the following lower bounds: $k_n > \frac{p_n}{\ln^2 p_n} \left( \ln p_n - 2.25 \right)$ for all $n \geq 2$, and $k_n > \frac{p_n}{\ln^2 p_n} \left( \ln p_n - 4.25 \right)$ for all $n \geq 7$.

This paper introduces a new, unsupervised learning-based framework for robust autonomous navigation in unstructured and cluttered environments. Recognizing that standard sensors often struggle with navigation duties due to adverse conditions like darkness, dust, or rain, the proposed solution employs a multi-modal input strategy to overcome these limitations. The system utilizes a combination of monocular RGB images, depth data from a RGB-D sensor, and LiDAR point clouds. The core of the framework involves a multi-object segmentation network designed to identify and separate navigable areas from obstacles within the LiDAR data. Subsequently, a specialized navigation network utilizes the segmentation results derived from the multi-modal inputs to compute the optimal path forward. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through extensive testing on both simulated and real-world datasets.

The discovery of a population of celestial bodies with neutral-sloped spectra has prompted speculation regarding their composition. While it is possible that these objects are covered in neutral-sloped dust mantles overlying standard ice mixtures, alternative hypotheses suggest they consist of constituents with inherently neutral reflectance properties. This study aims to determine the feasibility of forming such spectra through a mixture of silicate and carbonaceous materials with ice, utilizing radiative transfer modeling. We modeled scenarios involving varying abundances of 0.1, 0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 micrometer absorbing features found in silicate and carbonaceous sils, combined with water ice. Our simulations indicate that combining these rock types with water ice can successfully generate a neutral slope. However, the specific mixture ratios required to match the observed spectral features of neutral-sloped bodies are unlikely given current knowledge of the relative abundances of these ices and rocks within the outer Solar System. Consequently, the most plausible explanation remains the presence of a dust mantle composed of extraneous material draped over conventional ice compositions.

Let $T_n(q)$ represent the ring consisting of all $n \times n$ lower triangular matrices over the vector space $V = \mathbb{F}_q$, where $q$ is a prime power. The projective geometry $PG(T_n(q))$ is defined as the collection of all right submodules of $V$ that are not free cyclic modules. Within this geometry, points correspond to non-free cyclic submodules of rank $1$, while lines are defined as maximal right submodules with a specific structure. This document provides a complete characterization of incidence relations concerning points and lines in $PG(T_n(q))$, and it examines the lines incident to points that belong to a given right submodule.

The paper examines the interplay among the continuum's cardinal characteristics and determines the axiomatic status of $\mathbb{Q}$-generic filters over $\omega$ for both Cohen and real numbers. In the Cohen real model, specifically where Martin's Axiom holds relative to an inaccessible cardinal, the study demonstrates that one can derive $\sigma$-generic filters for both types of reals. The $\sigma$-rule remains applicable to the construction of these reals. The author shows that a single inaccessible cardinal is sufficient to establish the consistency of $\sigma$-generic filters for both Cohen and real numbers. The proof utilizes a novel method to build a single-step extension that adds a real, which can then be adapted to generate an equivalent result for the Cohen real case.

This study introduces a new class of Bayesian methods for learning dynamic treatment regimes, grounded in the pessimism principle to mitigate the impact of offline data noise. By employing conditional average potential as its objective function, this strategy inherently seeks to maximize average treatment benefits while favoring conservative choices under uncertainty. A key innovation is the integration of a novel offline Bayesian updater that combines a variational approximation with a reparameterization trick, enabling efficient posterior inference. Crucially, this updater successfully balances exploration and exploitation by making future decisions that acknowledge data limitations. Through extensive simulations, the proposed online pessimistic Bayesian approach outperforms both standard Bayesian and frequent techniques, demonstrating superior effectiveness in optimizing dynamic treatment sequences.

This study establishes a generalized formulation of Miyashita duality for tilting modules within the framework of Artin algebras and introduces an extended concept of duality for $R$-$R$ bimodules satisfying specific criteria, denoted as $\mathcal{D}_R(M)$, where applicable. Leveraging this duality framework, we prove the existence of corresponding property for $R$-$R$ bimodules satisfying the requisite conditions, exemplified by $\mathcal{D}_R(\mathrm{Tr}_R D R)$. Furthermore, we demonstrate the equivalence between the algebraic condition wherein every $R$-$R$ bimodule admits an exact sequence of the form $0 \to R \to P_0 \to P_1$ with $R$ projective components, and where every $R$-$R$ bimodule admits an exact sequence of the form $0 \to R \to P_0 \to P_1$ with $R$ projective components. Finally, we investigate the interrelations among various iterations of the functor $\mathcal{D}_R(-)$ applied to $R$.

The Kervaire-Milnor group, denoted as $E_{K M}$, represents the 16-dimensional integral cohomology of the 17-dimensional Kervaire manifold, which is an exotic sphere-like structure. Its dimensionality is dictated by the root system of the $E_8$ Lie algebra, which is visualized through a specific graph. This graph features 14 nodes arranged in a central square with 12 additional nodes extending from the central square's sides.

This study investigates the low-energy excitations of a two-dimensional flat-band superconductor, defined by nearest-neighbor hopping and the nearest-neighbor pair-hopping term. We demonstrate that the Hamiltonian can be mapped onto a model featuring only a U(1) symmetry, thereby preventing the emergence of the charge-2e Nambu mode typically associated with pair-hopping. Consequently, while the system forms a d-wave superconductor where unpaired electrons remain stationary, it supports mobile composite fermions carrying a charge of +e. Furthermore, we prove that the ground state exhibits long-range d-wave order, and we derive the dispersion of these composite fermions, which is determined by the parameters of the flat-band superconductor.

Presence-absence data, which indicate whether a species occupies a specific site, are extensively utilized in ecology. While such data are typically analyzed using logistic regression, this method often fails to capture the intricate inter-species interactions found in biological systems. Furthermore, standard models struggle with the "zero-inflation" common in species count data and frequently overlook the vital role of environmental covariates. Addressing these limitations, this study introduces a novel Bayesian framework designed for multivariate logistic regression of presence-absence data. This method models inter-species correlations through a factor structure, incorporates species-environment relationships via diagonal covariance matrices, and includes a specific zero-inflated process. Simulation experiments and an analysis of real-world data for the Kelp Forest Community in California demonstrate that this approach effectively reveals complex interaction patterns while accounting for the challenges of sparse zeros and environmental covariates.

Saloent object detection (SOD) aims to highlight significant areas within an image, a task that is vital for numerous downstream applications. While Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have significantly advanced the field, existing methods often fail to effectively capture contextual information, especially in complex scenes. To address this limitation, we introduce a novel Cross-Attention Context Extraction (CACE) module. By integrating a cross-attention mechanism, CACE enhances the highlighter's focus on salient areas through multi-scale contextual integration. Specifically, spatial attention refines the object's internal structure, while a reciprocal cross-attention workflow enables bidirectional information exchange between local details and global boundaries. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach surpasses current state-of-the-art methods across multiple benchmarks. Additionally, the module proves highly versatile, yielding promising outcomes in auxiliary tasks such as instance segmentation and object recognition.

This study outlines our participation in SemEval-2019 Task 6, which involved identifying various forms of abuse in Twitter posts. To address this challenge, we fine-tuned a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) based classifier utilizing both English and Spanish training data. This model achieved the top rank for the Subtask 2A and for both Subtask 2B and 2C, securing first and second places respectively.

A positive integer is defined as palindromic in base $b$ if its representation in that base forms a palindrome; notably, every even-length palindromic number in base $b \ge 3$ is divisible by its base. This paper investigates sums of distinct even-length distinct palindromic numbers from base 10 and from base 2. Specifically, for distinct elements $x_1, \dots, x_k$ chosen from the set of base 10 palindromes, we prove that their sum $x_1 + \dots + x_k$ is never itself a base 10 palindrome. Similarly, we demonstrate that no finite sum of distinct even-length binary palindromes equals another binary palindromic number.

Polyenergetic X-ray sources, such as those found in CT scanners, lead to beam hardening because lower-energy photons are preferentially absorbed, causing the effective energy of the beam to rise as it penetrates deeper into an object. This phenomenon results in non-linear relationships between X-ray attenuation and image intensity, potentially producing artefacts like ring patterns, shading, or cupping. While prior research has addressed polyenergetic effects using methods such as dual-energy techniques or iterative reconstruction, this work introduces a novel approach based on the Radon transform for tomographic image synthesis. This new method models the complex interactions between X-rays and matter by defining a energy-dependent linear relationship for X-ray paths, where the slope corresponds to the object's density and the intercept represents an effective X-ray energy. By inverting this process, the density of the object can be reconstructed. The proposed algorithm was validated through simulations and experiments involving phantoms, with results demonstrating its accuracy and the effective removal of both beam-hardening artefacts and cupping effects.

This paper introduces a handwriting recognition system designed for low-resource settings, with a specific focus on challenging, under-represented scripts found in historical records. We demonstrate the feasibility of developing a functional HTR for a rare, centuries-old manuscript using a newly created dataset of 1,000 pages from an 18th-century Irish Catholic seminary. This manuscript features a unique, cursive script that blends Gaelic and Latin elements. We evaluate the performance of current state-of-the-art models against this script and identify specific areas for future enhancements.

This study presents an analysis of the maximal angular momentum truncation parameter ($J_{\text{max}}$) in atomic nucleus computations utilizing the interacting boson model (IBM-3). By examining energy shifts in the first excited triplet state ($E(3^+_{\text{max}})$) across various proton and neutron counts, we have mapped the $E(3^+_{\text{max}})$ values on a two-dimensional chart. This approach identifies specific regions in the chart where the required $J_{\text{max}}$ values for accurate IBM-3 modeling exhibit abrupt changes. Our findings indicate that $J_{\text{max}}$ remains largely constant for most nuclei but undergoes a sharp increase in the $N=50$ and $N=82$ neutron shells. This phenomenon is attributed to the enhanced influence of the $\mathcal{O}(N_b)$ term in the IBM-3 Hamiltonian for these magic-number isotopes, where boson number $O$ scales significantly.

The Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model serves as a quintessential framework for exploring topology in one-dimensional systems. While traditionally analyzed using bulk topology—calculating Chern numbers or Zak phases to identify phases and determine critical points—this approach faces limitations near phase transitions, where such indicators fail as the bulk becomes non-finite. In these critical regions, the system exhibits scale invariance, rendering bulk properties insufficient for full characterization. To address this, we introduce methods for analyzing the intrinsic topology of SSH model critical points. Our work involves computing a topological invariant specific to 1D critical systems, examining the chiral charge and spectral flow, and achieving a complete topological characterization through the 2D expansion of the SSH system.

This paper investigates the compactness properties of composition operators defined on the Bergman spaces of specific bounded convex domains within $\mathbb{C}^n$, particularly those featuring non-trivial analytic automorphism groups and including ellipsoids, as well as the complex hyperbolic disk in $\mathbb{C}^2$.
